features.quote: In the east ... large courtyards, cisterns, and several stone troughs
On the southern side ... rooms with a cistern
North of the tower ... a hewn basin with a rough relief
About 0.2 km west of the site ... two stone sarcophagoi
On the slope east of the site ... several plundered burial caves
4. the concentration of sarcophagi and the cemetery

notes: Positions: words wherever the text gives a direction from the site. Fig. 492 (north arrow up, bar 0-200 m = 116 px) was measured from the camp centre (unit grid = entry grid 1997/1887): pool at ~57 deg, ~370 m (text: 0.2 km east; words used); burial caves at ~115 deg, ~530 m (text: east; words used); the separate label '4 Cemetery' at ~161 deg, ~310 m, coded as s2f9 with a plan position. s2f9 may overlap s2f7 (the caption groups the sarcophagi with the cemetery) but the text puts the sarcophagi 0.2 km west, so it is kept separate. s2f2 (header count and 'numerous cisterns') probably includes s2f3-s2f5. s2f6 is a hewn basin in a hall north of the central tower (southern third of the camp); no size, so pool_def unclear. Fig. 488 shows small unlabelled circles; not coded. Pool date D because the entry attributes it to the Roman camp (2nd c. CE, Hadrianic coins), not from a site period list. Stone troughs not coded (troughs excluded).
